chunks: From him, from al-Abdi, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from al-Askari (peace be upon him), who said:

"When the boy reaches eight years, his affair regarding his wealth is valid, and the obligations of fixed shares and limits have become incumbent upon him. And when the girl completes seven years, it is the same."
ai.seo_question: What is the age of legal maturity for boys and girls in Shia fiqh regarding financial transactions and religious obligations?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Askari (AS) clarifies the distinction between the onset of general religious obligations (taklif) and the capacity for independent financial management (rushd) in Shia fiqh. It establishes that while boys and girls become subject to hudud and fara'id at ages eight and seven respectively, their financial transactions are deemed valid from that same age, reflecting the early maturity of the female gender in this specific legal context. This view is foundational in the Ja'fari school for determining when a child's property can be managed without a guardian's direct intervention for validity.
